findings.issue: The newly admitted formal-team QUEUE path combines results using the last turn's baseCommitHash. A first turn can modify files outside its ownership scope and a second turn can modify only allowed files, causing ownership and verification checks to exclude the first turn while merging both commits. Preserve the initial execution base when combining runs.

Control lineage is looked up only by the current executionId, but deferred free-only review creates a new execution ID and PendingReview does not retain the original control execution. After reviewer recovery, including after rebase, the final ready bundle and merge receipt omit previously delivered control request/delivery hashes. Persist and propagate the original control execution separately from the new team admission.

summary: Fixed high-severity ownership bypass caused by QUEUE narrowing the commit range and medium-severity loss of control receipts when deferred or rebased review starts a new execution. Four regressions failed before fixes and now pass, including fail-closed handling for legacy pending records without source execution. Build, typecheck and 174 focused tests pass; the full suite had one Windows EPERM temporary-directory cleanup failure (2797 passed), and that unchanged runtime test passed on rerun.
